key_insight: Assemblies of intrinsically curved filaments can self-lock without friction through competition between elastic resistance to shape change and repulsive contact forces.
engineering_relevance: Filament curvature and bundle size offer design levers for cohesive structures and stimuli-responsive materials that assemble or disassemble without adhesive bonds.
method: Analyze a friction-free model of intrinsically helical filament assemblies.
Relate overcrowding-induced elastic prestress to self-locking or propagating detanglement fronts.
Test a generalized fracture criterion using experiments and simulations with frictional filaments.
evidence_signal: Experiments and simulations support the role of shape-elastic costs in self-locking and identify bundled structures that cannot self-lock at any friction level.
watch_item: Self-locking depends on filament number and preferred shape; friction alone cannot stabilize every bundle geometry.
paper_title: No friction required: Self-locking in entangled assemblies of curved filaments
